validity.recommendation: none — existence, classification, ownership and the Dikanka-cluster duplicate question all clear; length has a separate open spec concern (see other validity entry)
validity.researcher_notes:
EXISTENCE: confirmed by 2 independent, mutually corroborating sources. (1) Novosti Ukrainy (novostiukrainy.ru), 1 Jul 2011, republishing a Poltavshchyna wire item: on 29 June 2011 Ukrtransgaz began connecting a 12 km looping section on the 'Диканька — Кременчуг — Кривой Рог' ('Dikanka-Kremenchuk-Kryvyi Rih') mainline; the item's background note states the line has design capacity 3.2 bcm/y at 5.5 MPa, total length 272.2 km, and supplies industrial and residential consumers in Poltava and Kirovograd oblasts and Kryvyi Rih (Dnipropetrovsk oblast). (2) VNIPItransgaz (АО «ИПП «ВНИПИТРАНСГАЗ», vtg.com.ua) — a Russian/Soviet gas-pipeline design institute — publishes its own client-project table of trunk lines it engineered; it lists 'Диканька-Кременчуг-Кривой Рог' as a standalone line, 700 mm, 5.4 MPa, Ukraine, 1 string. Two structurally independent origins (a Ukrainian news wire vs. a pipeline design institute's own portfolio page) both name this exact pipeline by its full three-place name — this is not a GEM-only entity. Wiki-cited leads: the sheet's own gem.wiki page cited these same two URLs (both dead at their original addresses, both recovered via Wayback) plus a generic tsoua.com 'key facts' page and a generic LinkedIn company page (neither names this pipeline specifically, so neither counts toward existence on its own, but tsoua.com is useful for the ownership fact below).
CLASSIFICATION: correct as recorded — this is a state gas-transmission trunk (not a gathering/feeder line), explicitly described by source (1) as supplying industrial and residential gas consumers across three oblasts.
DUPLICATE / CLUSTER CHECK (per scope guidance on the 'Dikanka family' P1452/P1453/P1454/P1460 and the Kremenchuk-Kryvyi Rih corridor vs P0783): CLEARED, not a duplicate. VNIPItransgaz's table happens to independently corroborate the whole local cluster and shows Dikanka functioning as a multi-line HUB, not a single relabeled pipeline: it lists 'Ефремовка-Диканька-Киев' (1000 mm, 477.8 km — matches GEM P1453's 477.0 km almost exactly) and 'Шебелинка-Диканька-Киев' (in its table keyed to 1000 mm, 522 km — matches GEM P1454's 522.0 km exactly, though P1454's own diameter field '1200, 2350' looks like a separate typo unrelated to this row) as lines converging on Dikanka FROM the north/east and heading to Kyiv, while 'Диканька-Кременчуг-Кривой Рог' (our P1460) is listed as a wholly separate entry (different diameter, different destination — Kryvyi Rih, not Kyiv) heading south. Likewise P0783 (Yelets-Kremenchuk-Kryvyi Rih, 1420 mm, 771 km) is listed by VNIPItransgaz as two Russia-origin segments (619 km @ 1400 mm + 152 km @ 1200 mm = 771 km, matching P0783's total exactly) that are structurally distinct from our 700 mm all-Ukraine line — a parallel higher-capacity transit trunk sharing the same corridor terminus, not the same pipe. Both clearances are independently sourced, not just my own inference.
ATTRIBUTION: Owner1 = 'Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine' (100%) is correct and consistent with the country-standing rule — TSOU's own site (Wayback capture) states LLC Gas TSO of Ukraine has been the certified, fully independent GTS operator since 1 Jan 2020, with 100% of its equity transferred to Ukraine's Ministry of Energy on 27 Oct 2023. No Gazprom ownership recorded or warranted for this wholly domestic line.
CAVEAT: the line-specific technical evidence (source 1) is from 2011 — 15 years old. I found no evidence of damage, decommissioning, or mothballing of this specific line, and its route (Poltava/Kirovohrad/Dnipropetrovsk oblasts) is well outside occupied territory and the active front, so Status=operating stands, but the dedicated source is old and a more recent citation would strengthen it.

validity.recommendation: verify LengthKnown: the current sheet value (272.2 km) is corroborated exactly by one independent source (novostiukrainy, 2011) but contradicted by a second independent source (VNIPItransgaz's own project table, 236 km) for the same named 700 mm line — do not treat either figure as settled without reconciling the gap; check whether GEM's 272.2 km already includes post-1980s extensions to Kryvyi Rih that VNIPItransgaz's original design-institute figure predates, or whether the two names actually cover slightly different termini
validity.researcher_notes: Sheet: LengthKnown = 272.20 km. Source (1) novostiukrainy.ru (2011, quoting a Poltavshchyna wire item) states the pipeline's 'общая протяженность' (total length) is exactly 272.2 km — an EXACT match to the current GEM value. Source (2) VNIPItransgaz's (vtg.com.ua) own client-project table, in the same row that gives this line's diameter as 700 mm (which matches GEM exactly), gives its length as 236 km — a material ~13% (36.2 km) shortfall against both GEM and source (1). Both sources are independent of each other and of GEM (a Ukrainian news wire vs. a Russian/Soviet pipeline-engineering firm's own portfolio), and both unambiguously name the same three-place pipeline ('Dikanka-Kremenchuk-Kryvyi Rih' / 'Диканька-Кременчуг-Кривой Рог'), so this is a genuine value conflict, not a matching artifact. I could not resolve which figure is correct within this pass — plausible explanations (VNIPItransgaz's figure being an as-built design-era length before later Ukrainian-era extensions toward Kryvyi Rih, vs. GEM/source-1's figure including those extensions) are speculative and unverified. Note the 2011 12 km loop cited in source (1) is a parallel capacity-adding segment, not a route extension, so it does not by itself explain the 36 km gap. Flagging rather than resolving, per instructions not to silently pass a material disagreement.

fills.researcher_notes: Status inferred from context (per confidence_tiers.md, not a literal substring requirement): the source describes active gas-supply operation and a capacity-adding looping project being commissioned on this line, i.e. it was in service. Source explicitly calls it 'магистральный газопровод' (main gas pipeline) and describes it providing 'газоснабжение' (gas supply).

Source states 'проектной производительностью 3,2 млрд куб. м в год' (design capacity 3.2 bcm/year) — exact match to GEM's 3.20 bcm/y. Single source only (VNIPItransgaz's table does not list capacity), so tier medium rather than high.

Exact match to a real, verified source ('общая протяженность 272,2 км'), but see the paired validity concern: an independent second source (VNIPItransgaz) gives 236 km for the same named line, a material 36 km disagreement I could not reconcile. Tier kept at low, not medium, because of that unresolved conflict — do not read this ref as closing the question.
VNIPItransgaz's own project table lists 'Диканька-Кременчуг-Кривой Рог' at 700 mm — exact match. Only one source explicitly gives diameter (novostiukrainy does not), so tier medium.

Both endpoints (Dikanka start, Kryvyi Rih end) are named directly in the pipeline's full title in both independent sources — 2 independent sources agree, so tier high. Ukraine, both ends, per sources.

summary: P1460 confirmed real and correctly classified/attributed via 2 independent sources (novostiukrainy 2011 + VNIPItransgaz project table); Dikanka-cluster and Kremenchuk-Kryvyi Rih corridor duplicate checks CLEARED; 1 open spec concern — LengthKnown 272.2 km (GEM) vs 236 km (VNIPItransgaz), unresolved, flagged.
